evenity_postmenopausal.section_title:
1.1 
Treatment of Postmenopausal Women with Osteoporosis at High Risk for Fracture
evenity_postmenopausal.quote_exact:
1.1 
Treatment of Postmenopausal Women with Osteoporosis at High Risk for Fracture 
 
EVENITY is indicated for the treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women at high risk for 
fracture, defined as a history of osteoporotic fracture, or multiple risk factors for fracture; or patients who 
have failed or are intolerant to other available osteoporosis therapy.

evenity_limitations.quote_exact:
1.2 
Limitations of Use 
 
The anabolic effect of EVENITY wanes after 12 monthly doses of therapy. Therefore, the duration of 
EVENITY use should be limited to 12 monthly doses. If osteoporosis therapy remains warranted, 
continued therapy with an anti-resorptive agent should be considered [see Dosage and Administration 
(2.2) and Clinical Studies (14.1)].

prolia_postmenopausal.section_title:
1.1 
Treatment of Postmenopausal Women with Osteoporosis at High Risk for Fracture
prolia_postmenopausal.quote_exact:
1.1 
Treatment of Postmenopausal Women with Osteoporosis at High Risk for Fracture 
 
Prolia is indicated for the treatment of postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high risk for fracture, 
defined as a history of osteoporotic fracture, or multiple risk factors for fracture; or patients who have 
failed or are intolerant to other available osteoporosis therapy.  In postmenopausal women with 
osteoporosis, Prolia reduces the incidence of vertebral, nonvertebral, and hip fractures [see Clinical 
Studies (14.1)].

prolia_men.section_title:
1.2 
Treatment to Increase Bone Mass in Men with Osteoporosis
prolia_men.quote_exact:
1.2 
Treatment to Increase Bone Mass in Men with Osteoporosis  
 
Prolia is indicated for treatment to increase bone mass in men with osteoporosis at high risk for fracture, 
defined as a history of osteoporotic fracture, or multiple risk factors for fracture; or patients who have 
failed or are intolerant to other available osteoporosis therapy [see Clinical Studies (14.2)].

prolia_glucocorticoid.quote_exact:
1.3 
Treatment of Glucocorticoid-Induced Osteoporosis 
 
Prolia is indicated for the treatment of glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis in men and women at high 
risk of fracture who are either initiating or continuing systemic glucocorticoids in a daily dosage 
equivalent to 7.5 mg or greater of prednisone and expected to remain on glucocorticoids for at least 
6 months.  High risk of fracture is defined as a history of osteoporotic fracture, multiple risk factors for 
fracture, or patients who have failed or are intolerant to other available osteoporosis therapy [see Clinical 
Studies (14.3)].

amjevita_ra.quote_exact:
1.1 
Rheumatoid Arthritis  
 
AMJEVITA is indicated for reducing signs and symptoms, inducing major clinical response, 
inhibiting the progression of structural damage, and improving physical function in adult patients 
with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis. AMJEVITA can be used alone or in 
combination with methotrexate or other non-biologic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs 
(DMARDs).

avsola_ra.quote_exact:
1.5 
Rheumatoid Arthritis 
 
AVSOLA, in combination with methotrexate, is indicated for reducing signs and symptoms, inhibiting the 
progression of structural damage, and improving physical function in adult patients with moderately to 
severely active rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

enbrel_ra.quote_exact:
1.1 
Rheumatoid Arthritis  
 
Enbrel is indicated for reducing signs and symptoms, inducing major clinical response, inhibiting the progression of 
structural damage, and improving physical function in patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid 
arthritis (RA).  Enbrel can be initiated in combination with methotrexate (MTX) or used alone.

riabni_ra.quote_exact:
1.3 
Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA)  
 
RIABNI, in combination with methotrexate, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with 
moderately- to-severely- active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response to one or 
more TNF antagonist therapies.

amjevita_psa.quote_exact:
1.3 
Psoriatic Arthritis  
 
AMJEVITA is indicated for reducing signs and symptoms, inhibiting the progression of 
structural damage, and improving physical function in adult patients with active psoriatic 
arthritis. 
AMJEVITA can be used alone or in combination with non-biologic DMARDs.

avsola_psa.quote_exact:
1.7 
Psoriatic Arthritis 
 
AVSOLA is indicated for reducing signs and symptoms of active arthritis, inhibiting the progression of 
structural damage, and improving physical function in adult patients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA).

enbrel_psa.quote_exact:
1.3 
Psoriatic Arthritis  
 
Enbrel is indicated for reducing signs and symptoms, inhibiting the progression of structural damage of active 
arthritis, and improving physical function in adult patients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA).  Enbrel can be used with or 
without methotrexate.

otezla_psa.quote_exact:

Psoriatic Arthritis 
 
OTEZLA is indicated for the treatment of adult patients and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older 
and weighing at least 20 kg with active psoriatic arthritis. 
 
OTEZLA XR is indicated for the treatment of adult patients and pediatric patients 6 years of age and 
older and weighing at least 50 kg with active psoriatic arthritis.

enbrel_juvenile_psa.quote_exact:
1.6 
Juvenile Psoriatic Arthritis  
 
Enbrel is indicated for the treatment of active juvenile psoriatic arthritis (JPsA) in pediatric patients 2 years of age 
and older.

tezspire_asthma.quote_exact:

TEZSPIRE is indicated for the add-on maintenance treatment of adult and pediatric 
patients aged 12 years and older with severe asthma.
Limitations of Use:
TEZSPIRE is not indicated for the relief of acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus.

bkemv_warning_within_section1.quote_exact:
1.3 
Generalized Myasthenia Gravis (gMG) 
 
BKEMV is indicated for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are 
anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive. 
WARNING: SERIOUS MENINGOCOCCAL INFECTIONS 
 
Eculizumab products, complement inhibitors, increase the risk of serious infections caused 
by Neisseria meningitidis [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1)]. Life-threatening and fatal 
meningococcal infections have occurred in patients treated with complement inhibitors. 
These infections may become rapidly life-threatening or fatal if not recognized and treated 
early. 
 
Complete or update vaccination for meningococcal bacteria (for serogroups A, C, W, Y, 
and B) at least 2 weeks prior to the first dose of BKEMV, unless the risks of delaying 
therapy with BKEMV outweigh the risk of developing a serious infection. Comply with 
the most current Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) 
recommendations for vaccinations against meningococcal bacteria in patients receiving a 
complement inhibitor. See Warnings and Precautions (5.1) for additional guidance on the 
management of the risk of serious infections caused by meningococcal bacteria. 
 
Patients receiving eculizumab products are at increased risk for invasive disease caused 
by Neisseria meningitidis, even if they develop antibodies following vaccination. Monitor 
patients for early signs and symptoms of serious meningococcal infections and evaluate 
immediately if infection is suspected. 
Because of the risk of serious meningococcal infections, BKEMV is available only through a 
restricted program under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) called 
BKEMV REMS [see Warnings and Precautions (5.2)].

extraction_findings.finding: PAVBLU Section 1 states the predicate; Sections 1.1 through 1.4 are only disease headings. All four headings have unresolved_heading_only. A block-only predicate matcher loses all four valid Section 1 indications.
Inherited section titles on next-page page-number fragments can match condition names despite having no indication content. Group meaningful continuations and do not cite page-number-only fragments.

TEZSPIRE Section 1.1 is complete prose with a positive maintenance indication and an explicit acute limitation, but carries unresolved_figure. Broad warning filtering can remove the only asthma indication.
AMJEVITA ulcerative-colitis indication in Section 1.6 p4 has a Limitations of Use continuation on p5. General indication assembly should retain same-section meaningful continuation.

EPOGEN Section 1.4 heading is split into an r001 block and a continuation; its indicated sentence ends on the following page, followed immediately by a not-indicated sentence. Parent section and page-continuation assembly must preserve these boundaries.
BKEMV Section 1.3 contains its gMG indication followed by WARNING: SERIOUS MENINGOCOCCAL INFECTIONS. Section 1 membership alone does not make every condition named in the block an indication.
Only AIMOVIG, OTEZLA, RIABNI contain the word migraine anywhere in this corpus. Only AIMOVIG contains it in Section 1. OTEZLA and RIABNI occurrences are adverse-reaction evidence.

validation_rules: Every evidence quote is an exact SourceBlock.text, with SHA-256 and original archive spans.
Every positive expected product has affirmative Section 1 indication evidence; PAVBLU evidence is composed from its Section 1 parent and child.
Negative expected sets are local support absence or explicit label limitation, not universal clinical claims.
Broad-condition matches must preserve population/use/combinational qualifiers; lexical mention alone is insufficient.

fixture_origin.expectations: The 12 case product sets and 31 evidence blocks are frozen from the pre-calibration source audit; wording variants do not change expectations.

measurement_limits: Exact returned product sets and the first displayed evidence for each expected product are graded; PAVBLU uses its explicitly audited contiguous parent/condition-heading pair.
This does not measure clinical precision of every returned passage, generated answers, or whether the supplied labels are current.
PAVBLU requires its audited parent and DME heading as the first adjacent same-product/document/XML source pair, with exact quotes and spans; either fragment alone fails.
Expected identities never become retrieval filters. All query variants run separately with the same frozen expected set.
